I would handle scalability, synchronization, and authentication in an offline messaging app by using a combination of local storage, a robust backend architecture, and standard security protocols. First, for scalability, I would implement a microservices architecture on the backend, allowing different parts of the app, like message handling or user management, to scale independently as the user base grows. Second, synchronization would be managed using a conflict-free replicated data type approach, ensuring that when a user comes back online, their local changes merge correctly with the server data without data loss. Finally, authentication would be secured using industry-standard token-based authentication, like OAuth 2.0, to ensure that only verified users can access their data.

The tradeoff here is complexity; implementing CRDTs and microservices adds significant initial development overhead. However, this complexity is necessary to guarantee a good user experience, especially when dealing with intermittent connectivity. For implementation, the Android app would use a local database like Room to store messages offline, and upon reconnection, it would push updates to the server via a background service.

In conclusion, this layered approach ensures the app remains fast and usable offline while remaining secure and capable of handling large numbers of users online.

I would measure latency by tracking the time difference between sending the request to https://example.com/api/v1 and receiving the first chunk of the AI response, and then monitoring the time between subsequent chunks. To handle serialization, I would use a streaming JSON parser that processes data as it arrives, rather than waiting for the entire response body to download. For concurrency, I would implement asynchronous network calls using Kotlin Coroutines to ensure the UI remains responsive while the data is being streamed.

The main trade-off here is complexity versus responsiveness; using a streaming parser adds complexity compared to simple blocking calls, but it is necessary for a good user experience. I would ensure that the `client_id` is passed correctly in the request headers to maintain session context during the stream. In summary, by combining asynchronous streaming with precise timing measurements, I can effectively manage the performance aspects of the AI response.
